name: Philippians

overview.author: The apostle Paul, with Timothy (1:1).
overview.date: About AD 60–62, during Paul’s imprisonment, likely in Rome.
overview.audience: The church in Philippi, the first church Paul planted in Europe (Acts 16), which had supported him financially.
overview.setting: Paul writes from prison, uncertain whether he will live or die, thanking the Philippians for their gift sent through Epaphroditus.
overview.purpose: To thank the Philippians, encourage joy and steadfastness in suffering, urge humility and unity by Christ’s example, warn against false teachers, and teach contentment in Christ.
overview.structure: Paul’s circumstances and joy (1), Christ’s humility as our example (2), knowing Christ above all (3), and peace and contentment (4).

themes.title: Joy
themes.text: Paul uses “joy” and “rejoice” repeatedly while in chains.

themes.title: Partnership in the Gospel
themes.text: The Philippians shared in Paul’s ministry from the first day.

themes.title: Christ’s Humility
themes.text: Christ emptied Himself, took the form of a servant, and died on a cross.

themes.title: Unity
themes.text: Stand firm in one spirit, having the same mind.

themes.title: Knowing Christ
themes.text: Everything is loss compared to knowing Christ.

themes.title: Peace and Contentment
themes.text: Prayer brings God’s peace, and Christ gives strength for every situation.

christInBook.text: Christ, in the form of God, humbled Himself to death on a cross.
God highly exalted Him, and every knee will bow and every tongue confess Jesus Christ is Lord.
Righteousness comes from God through faith in Christ.
Our Savior will transform our lowly bodies like His glorious body.

crossReferences.note: The founding of the church in Philippi.
Setting our minds on things above.

reflection: Where do you need confidence that God will complete His good work in you (1:6)?
How would you finish the sentence “For to me to live is...”?
Where do you need the humility of Christ in a relationship (2:3–8)?
What have you counted as gain that you need to count as loss for Christ?
What anxiety can you turn into prayer with thanksgiving today (4:6–7)?

chapterList.title: To Live Is Christ
chapterList.summary: Paul thanks God for the Philippians’ partnership and is confident that God will complete His good work in them. He prays that their love will abound with knowledge. His imprisonment has advanced the gospel. “To live is Christ, and to die is gain.” He urges them to live worthy of the gospel and stand firm.
questions: How did Paul’s chains advance the gospel (1:12–14)?
What does it mean to live a life worthy of the gospel (1:27)?

chapterList.title: The Mind of Christ
chapterList.summary: Paul urges unity and humility: “count others more significant than yourselves.” Have the mind of Christ, who emptied Himself, became a servant, and was obedient to death on a cross; God exalted Him. Work out your salvation, for God works in you. Shine as lights. Paul commends Timothy and Epaphroditus.
questions: How does 2:6–11 describe Jesus’ humility and exaltation?
What does it mean to “work out your salvation” (2:12–13)?
How do Timothy and Epaphroditus model Christlike service?

chapterList.title: Knowing Christ
chapterList.summary: Paul warns against those who put confidence in the flesh. He had every credential but counts it all loss “because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.” He wants a righteousness from God through faith. He presses on toward the goal. “Our citizenship is in heaven.”
questions: What did Paul once rely on (3:4–6)?
What does it mean to press on toward the goal (3:12–14)?
How does heavenly citizenship shape earthly life (3:20–21)?

chapterList.title: Rejoice and Be Content
chapterList.summary: Paul urges two women to agree in the Lord. “Rejoice in the Lord always.” Do not be anxious but pray with thanksgiving, and God’s peace will guard your hearts. Think on what is true, honorable, and lovely. Paul has learned contentment: “I can do all things through him who strengthens me.” God will supply every need.
questions: What does Paul tell us to think about (4:8)?
What is the secret of contentment (4:11–13)?

tagline: Joy in Christ in every circumstance
readingPlan: 4 chapters: one chapter a day takes 4 days; two a day takes about 2 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
